To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the wavelength shifter coating of photomultiplier tubes increases their sensitivity by a factor of ∼3.5, and that the coating is a simple operation that does not damage the photomultiplier tube and can be done by anyone.

the coating procedure we have used is simple and effective; that the coated phototubes have a gain in photoelectron production by a factor of 3-4; and that the figure of merit for a gas Cherenkov system is increased by about the same factor.

(1) the Cherenkov radiation from the charged particle is detected by a photomultiplier tube (PMT), (2) the PMT is coated with a thin layer of a scintillator material, (3) the scintillator material absorbs the Cherenkov light and re-emits it at a longer wavelength, (4) the wavelength of the light emitted by the scintillator is absorbed by the PMT, which produces a larger number of photoelectrons,
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new type of Cherenkov detector, based on the use of a thin deposit of a wavelength shifter (scintillator) on the photocathode of a conventional photomultiplier (PMT).
the development of new techniques for the detection of ionizing radiation and charged particles, based upon the use of scintillators.
the design and fabrication of a novel class of photodetector based on the use of a thin layer of wavelength shifter deposited directly onto the photocathode.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the coating operation is straightforward, the coated phototubes perform well and are stable, the figure of merit is comparable to that of the best phototubes in use today.

, in spite of the many difficulties encountered during the development of the project, the results achieved are encouraging and show that a considerable improvement of the performances of the present generation of phototubes can be expected by using a thin layer of a scintillator as a wavelength shifter.
the use of a wavelength shifter on photomultiplier tubes is a very useful technique to increase the light collection in Cherenkov counters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of wavelength shifters is a very attractive technique in Cherenkov light detectors, particularly in those applications where large numbers of photoelectrons are required.

the use of a thin deposit of wavelength shifting material on photomultipliers of the XP1041 class (Philips), with a thin glass envelope, can be used with advantage to improve the performance of Cherenkov counters.
a Cherenkov light counter can be made to yield a factor 4 more photoelectrons than a standard photomultiplicr.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to improve the efficiency of photomultipliers by a factor of 3-4 with a very simple technique.
it is now possible to use a single wavelength-shifting layer to improve the performance of a Cherenkov counter.
the coating operation does not affect the gain and time resolution of the standard photomultipliers.
